description: Create the apps/kitchen Django app with its view, URL, and model-free architecture. Add a 'mark_ready' AJAX endpoint that transitions order status from 'preparing' → 'ready'. This feature depends on FEAT-001 (kitchen_staff_required decorator must exist). Independent of FEAT-003 (which handles templates and JS).
steps: 1. Create directory apps/kitchen/ with __init__.py, apps.py, views.py, urls.py. No models.py needed (kitchen app has no DB models). Create apps/kitchen/apps.py with KitchenConfig class: name='apps.kitchen', verbose_name='Kitchen'.

2. Create apps/kitchen/views.py with two views:
   - kitchen_orders(request): decorated with @login_required, @kitchen_staff_required (from apps.accounts.decorators). Queries Order.objects.filter(status='preparing').select_related('cashier').prefetch_related('items').order_by('queued_at', 'created_at'). Renders 'kitchen/orders.html' with context {'orders': orders}.
   - mark_order_ready(request, pk): decorated with @login_required, @kitchen_staff_required, @require_POST. Uses transaction.atomic() + select_for_update(). Validates order.status == 'preparing', calls validate_status_transition('preparing','ready',order=order) (imported from apps.orders.services), sets order.ready_at = timezone.now(), sets order.status='ready', order.save(). Calls log_action(request.user, 'order.mark_ready', order, detail='Kitchen staff marked order as ready.'). Returns JsonResponse({'success': True, 'order_number': order.order_number, 'new_status': 'ready'}). On failure returns JsonResponse({'success': False, 'error': str(e)}, status=400). Does NOT call broker.publish directly — the post_save signal in apps/realtime/signals.py already fires status_changed on every Order.save(), which notifies all subscribers including the kitchen stream.

3. Create apps/kitchen/urls.py:
   app_name = 'kitchen'
   urlpatterns = [
       path('', views.kitchen_orders, name='orders'),
       path('<int:pk>/ready/', views.mark_order_ready, name='mark_ready'),
   ]
4. In kape_de_manubag/settings.py: add 'apps.kitchen' to INSTALLED_APPS list after 'apps.chatbot'.
5. In kape_de_manubag/urls.py: add path('kitchen/', include('apps.kitchen.urls')) to urlpatterns. Place it after the existing app includes.
6. Create apps/kitchen/migrations/ directory with __init__.py only (no models = no migration file needed beyond the empty package).

7. In apps/realtime/views.py: add a new SSE endpoint kitchen_event_stream(request) decorated with @login_required, @kitchen_or_admin_required (from apps.accounts.decorators). It uses the same broker.subscribe()/unsubscribe() pattern as event_stream, but filters the events it forwards to only: 'status_changed' (where new_status == 'preparing' — order entered kitchen, or new_status == 'ready' — order left kitchen) and 'heartbeat'. This keeps kitchen clients from seeing financial events (new_order with totals, payment_confirmed, gcash_submitted, inventory_changed). The stream function yields format_sse for matching events and heartbeats every 20s. Add URL: in apps/realtime/urls.py, add path('kitchen-stream/', views.kitchen_event_stream, name='kitchen_event_stream').

8. In templates/base.html: add 'kitchen:orders' to window.KDM_URLS JS object: kitchenStream: '{% url "realtime:kitchen_event_stream" %}'. This URL reference must be conditionally rendered only when the URL resolves — wrap in try/except templatetag or add it unconditionally since it will always exist after FEAT-002.
acceptance_criteria: GET /kitchen/ returns 200 for kitchen_staff user, shows orders with status='preparing'
GET /kitchen/ for unauthenticated user redirects to /accounts/login/?next=/kitchen/
GET /kitchen/ for cashier/admin returns 403 or redirects to menu:index (kitchen_staff_required blocks non-kitchen roles)
POST /kitchen/<pk>/ready/ transitions a 'preparing' order to 'ready', sets ready_at, creates audit log entry
POST /kitchen/<pk>/ready/ on a non-'preparing' order returns 400 JSON error
GET /realtime/kitchen-stream/ returns SSE stream for kitchen_staff user
GET /realtime/kitchen-stream/ for unauthenticated returns redirect to login
python manage.py check runs clean (no system check errors)
verification: python manage.py migrate  (no-op, no new migrations needed for kitchen app)
python manage.py test apps.kitchen  (all tests pass)
python manage.py test apps.orders  (existing order tests still pass)
python manage.py test apps.realtime  (existing realtime tests still pass)
